idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the production deploy of v2.3.1. At time of detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1 with the service reporting unhealthy and an error rate of 18%.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.0 was the most recent release with a confirmed healthy production status in the deployment history (v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy). Note: v2.3.1-rc was excluded as it is a staging release and is itself marked unhealthy.

Rollback completed successfully with status "rolled_out" across all regions. Follow-up: confirm health check recovery and error rate normalization on v2.3.0, investigate the root cause of v2.3.1 failures, and hold further v2.3.1 promotion until remediated.

args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**1. Rollback — completed and verified**
- Diagnosis: `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an **18% error rate**.
- Target selection: from release history, v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). **v2.3.0** was the most recent release healthy *in production*. I deliberately excluded `v2.3.1-rc` — it's a staging release and it's also marked unhealthy, so it doesn't qualify.
- Action: rolled back `checkout-api` to **v2.3.0** across all production regions (`status: rolled_out`).
- Post-rollback check: service is now **healthy: true**, version v2.3.0 in us-east/us-west/eu-west, error rate down from 18% to **~0.2%**. Recovery confirmed.

**2. Incident — opened**
- **INC-0001**, SEV2, "checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0", status open, on-call paged.
- The first attempt timed out; I retried using the same idempotency key, so no duplicate incident was created. The successful second call returned incident ID INC-0001.

**One thing to flag:** `list_incidents` is currently returning an empty list even though the create call returned INC-0001 as open. This looks like read-model/replication lag rather than a failed write, but it's worth confirming the incident actually appears in the incident console — if it doesn't show up shortly, the create may need to be re-filed.

**Suggested follow-ups:** root-cause the v2.3.1 failures before any re-promotion, and check whether the 0.2% residual error rate is within the normal baseline for this service.
